## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Dutiyakāyappacālaka* ("16. Swaying the body") is the sixteenth training rule in the *Sekhiya* section of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* within the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule regulates monastic decorum regarding bodily conduct, specifically prohibiting unmindful swaying or swinging of the body [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule and its word commentary has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

The rule is widely attested across early Buddhist monastic codes [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali tradition, direct counterparts are found in the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (Sk 16), the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Sk 16), the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Sk 16), and the corresponding sections of both the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī *Parivāra* [SuttaCentral]. Parallels outside the Theravāda lineage are preserved in Chinese and Sanskrit across several vinaya recensions, including the Sarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, and Mūlasarvāstivāda traditions [SuttaCentral].
